translations.text: For this reason, now, just as every believer in every congregation that exists according to our way of life—or rather, everyone who fears the Lord in every place—acts boldly in all righteousness and every good deed, trampling down all lawlessness and every deceit,
so too a righteous king is courageous, together with those who belong to him, and is always among them.

And whenever their enemies come to fight against them and all those who belong to the king, they rise up against their enemies and overtake them, and they do not return until they have destroyed them.
This is also how it is whenever everyone, at all times, keeps the Lord’s commandments in every congregation, in every place throughout the whole earth: God is with them.

And whenever Satan rises up against them to wage war on them, they call upon the name of the King of glory, Jesus, the Lord, the mighty and strong one, the Lord who is powerful in battle. And he sends them help through his holy angels. Everyone with whom the Lord is present pursues the demonic enemies, and they do not return until they have wiped out Satan and all his other evil deeds.

For this reason, just as all our holy fathers, from righteous Abel down to today, drove Satan and every evil deed out of themselves, their congregations, their sons, their daughters, their brothers, their companions, and everyone who fears the Lord and who had received instruction and obeyed them in everything,

so too, now and forever, everyone who keeps God’s commandments drives the Satans and all their other deeds out of themselves, like those who pursue robbers who want to plunder houses full of silver and gold. And they drive them out of their congregations, like those who pursue wild beasts that want to seize and scatter the sheep of the flock.

And they drive them out of their sons, their daughters, and their companions, like those who pursue foxes that want to destroy very fine vineyards, according to the Scriptures: “Catch for me little foxes that destroy the vineyards.”
And in the same way, they also drive them out of everyone who fears the Lord, receives their instruction, and keeps their words.
And this is how Moses spoke in anguish: “While I am still with you, you provoke God. How, then, will you not provoke him after my death?”
And great multitudes sinned after he had departed from them, and after he had instructed them with all his words, after they had seen many wonders.
And if, after all these things, we sinned before the Lord, not only in our fathers’ house, in our childhood and our ignorance, but also after we had received a share in the knowledge of the truth,
yet again, after some years, he turned back and denied the truth, though no one questioned him.
